rendered: The review does not really recommend tens of nanometres. The tens-of-nanometres figure describes what the literature usually reports, which the review treats as too thick. The reason is kinetic: ZrO2 has[1][2] lithium-ion diffusivity, so lithium transport through the coating becomes the bottleneck. Longer diffusion times are seen for thicker layers, and the review's own calculation puts the ideal thickness below ten nanometers[3] for better electrochemical performance. The literature figure is in most cases, is in the tens of nanometers[4] because thickness is hard to control with easily scalable processes.[5] The review's recommended ceiling for widely used cost-effective coatings is[6] around ∼10 nm[7] for effective use of their benefits. Thick inert layers also carry a side-reaction risk, since ZrO2 may react with lithium ions and form secondary phases, causing capacity fading.[8]
